# Coding-stage assessment

## Evidence and baseline

- The full pinned story (`user_story`, characters 0-16000) calls for a Python 3.12 Flask/Jinja server-rendered password-reset exercise, synthetic accounts, an in-memory notification sink, pytest, production-limitations documentation, and no deployment or deployment workflows.
- I inspected attached `sign-in-wireframe.png` (attachment `457acc5e-8bce-44d6-abec-d204c28e4d84`): a white background with a centered thin-bordered panel; bold **Sign in** heading; stacked, labeled **Email address** and **Password** fields with `name@example.com` and masked `********` placeholders; a blue underlined **Forgot password?** link beneath the password field; a wide dark **Sign in** button beneath the link; muted **No account? Contact your administrator.** footer. The image specifies neither exact CSS measurements nor a working sign-in destination or recovery-page appearance.
- The curated account recovery standard (`knowledge` source `28e06fb4-ccd1-4117-8f7b-b2a6c9bfaf1f`, locator `v1, chunk 0`) requires an account-independent reset-request response, five requests per account per hour, single-use links expiring 30 minutes after issuance, invalidation of every active session after reset, and notification of the owner after each successful reset.
- Approved prior outputs read through the platform: `requirements_analysis` (REQ-001 through REQ-018), `ui_analysis` (observed sign-in versus proposed recovery/accessibility details), `solution_design` (TASK-001 through TASK-006, architecture and pytest gate), `test_case_design` (TC-001 through TC-030), and `acceptance_20261028191242_8eaf7f_risk` (RD8CDC-001 through RD8CDC-006, prospective risks, not observed defects). The approved design and suggested mapping require T002 through T007 to retain their corresponding TASK-001 through TASK-006 identifiers.
- Repository baseline: only a short placeholder README, predecessor design documents and prior stage artifacts; no Flask application, tests, Python project manifest, lockfile, linter configuration or deployment workflow. The worktree is clean. `/usr/bin/python3.12` reports Python 3.12.3; `uv` is available, but Flask and pytest are not installed in this interpreter (`python3.12 -m pytest --version` fails with no module named pytest). No implemented behavior or passing gates can be claimed yet. No service is required: the approved exercise uses injected in-process state and notification sink, not a production identity, database, email or Docker service.

## Implementation and coverage implications

- Begin with a green Python scaffold and explicit root-level gates before implementing features: a Python 3.12 project/locked dependencies, README, `.gitignore`, a passing scaffold smoke test, then application tasks in approved dependency order. Design specifies `python3.12 -m pytest` as the test gate; a build/syntax check and lint/format check must be established as scaffold gates (for example `python3.12 -m compileall -q <package> tests` and a project-pinned Ruff check) and carried forward at checkpoints. Select concrete paths, versions and commands during planning; do not treat currently missing dependencies as failed product tests.
- TASK-001 covers REQ-001/002/013/014: application factory and server-rendered sign-in/request pages, observed visual hierarchy and working recovery entry. TASK-002 covers REQ-009/011/012: isolated synthetic hashed accounts, injected UTC clock, synchronized requests/tokens/session registry and private sink. TASK-003 covers REQ-003/004/005: normalized lookup, generic response equality, rolling-window cap and private opaque-link issuance. TASK-004 covers REQ-006 through REQ-010: digest-bound, issue-time-expiring single-use reset, atomic password/session/notice effects and non-success states. TASK-005 covers REQ-015 with traceable pytest cases. TASK-006 covers REQ-016/017/018 with production limitations and no-deployment/no-workflow evidence. Final reporting must map every TC-001 through TC-030 to automated tests or a justified manual check in `tests.json` and write `coding-report.md` in the run artifact folder.
- Key test boundaries: public status/body/navigation parity for existing, unknown and capped accounts; five accepted requests followed by a denied sixth and an exactly one-hour reopening; token expiry just before, exactly at, and after issue time plus 30 minutes; repeated and concurrent submissions; account isolation; two prior sessions of one owner versus another owner's session; exactly one private success notice per successful reset. Compare only otherwise equivalent submissions and keep token, email, password, link URL, inventory and sink data out of public output and logs. Accessibility and page semantics can be tested structurally; manual assistive-technology or visual checks should not be mislabeled as automated. TC-026 requires a complete delivery-action record to establish no deployment; if unavailable, record an evidence gap rather than claiming proof from repository absence.
- Treat the approved solution design as the bound: cryptographically random opaque tokens with private digest storage, precise timezone-aware UTC issuance time, check/write operations guarded by one lock, CSRF on POST, trusted link origin, escaped templates, secure secret/cookie configuration, and nonpublic synthetic state. GET does not consume links, and POST rechecks eligibility. Local locking cannot provide multi-worker or durable guarantees. No sign-in authentication/success route, recovery-page visual spec, password complexity rule, external notification service, production account integration or deployment target is authorized; use the design's nonempty new-password criterion and fixture-created sessions without inventing login behavior.
- Production limits to document: all account, request, token, session and sink state is volatile and process-local; restart loses it and workers do not coordinate. A production replacement would need transactional durable stores and outbox, real identity and message integrations, key/secret management, retention, abuse controls and operations/monitoring. None is part of this exercise. Never change `.github/workflows/`, deploy, or use real service credentials.

Assessment only: source files remain untouched. Dependency-ordered task planning, exact validation commands and approval follow in the next phase.
